passages.t: The mystery made known: Gentiles are fellow heirs
passages.happening:
Paul begins a prayer, “For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentiles...” (verse 1), and then breaks off to explain himself.

God gave him a task, ‘the stewardship of God’s grace’, and showed him a mystery (verses 2-3). It was not made known to earlier generations as it has now been revealed (verse 5). “This mystery is that through the gospel the Gentiles are fellow heirs, fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus” (verse 6).

Paul became a servant of this gospel by God's grace. “Though I am less than the least of all the saints, this grace was given me: to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ” (verse 8). God's purpose is that “now, through the church, the manifold wisdom of God should be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms” (verse 10).

In Christ, “we may enter God’s presence with boldness and confidence” (verse 12). So he asks them not to lose heart over his sufferings, which are for them (verse 13).
passages.hearers:
Paul is in chains because of the Gentiles. Acts tells how he was arrested in Jerusalem after he was accused of bringing a Gentile into the temple (Acts 21:27-29). His prison is the price of the very message he describes here.

‘Mystery’ had a sound in the Greek world. Certain cults were called ‘mysteries’: secret rites shown only to those who joined, who were sworn never to tell. Paul uses the word in a different way, as the book of Daniel does, for a secret of God that God himself makes known. A mystery in Paul is not kept hidden. It is a plan God kept until the right time, and now tells to everyone.

What is the mystery? That Gentiles share the inheritance with Israel, share the body, share the promise. Three words in Greek begin with the same prefix, ‘together-’: together-heirs, together-body, together-sharers. The Old Testament had promised that the nations would be blessed. What no one had seen was that they would be joined to Israel's Messiah as equals, in one body, without first becoming Jews.

‘Less than the least of all the saints’ is one unusual word in Greek, ‘least’ with ‘less’ added to it, something like ‘leaster’. He never forgot that he had persecuted the church.

Verse 10 is breathtaking. A church of former strangers, Jews and Gentiles at one table, is God's showcase to the powers of heaven. Its unity shows God's wisdom. Its divisions hide it.
passages.ot:
God promised Abraham from the start: “all the families of the earth will be blessed through you” (Genesis 12:3). And he told his servant in Isaiah, “I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth” (Isaiah 49:6).

The word ‘mystery’ comes from Daniel, where Daniel tells the king, “there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries” (Daniel 2:28). Paul uses the word the same way: God's secret, made known by God.
passages.asks: God means to show his wisdom through a church where former strangers belong together. Ask what your church shows the watching world, and the unseen powers: unity across old lines, or the same divisions as everywhere else. And Paul says believers may come to God ‘with boldness and confidence’. Ask how you come to him in prayer.

passages.t: ‘To know this love that surpasses knowledge’
passages.happening:
Now Paul finishes the prayer he began: “for this reason I bow my knees before the Father, from whom every family in heaven and on earth derives its name” (verses 14-15).

He asks that God will strengthen them “with power through His Spirit in your inner being, so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith” (verses 16-17). He prays that, rooted in love, they will be able “to comprehend the length and width and height and depth of the love of Christ, and to know this love that surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God” (verses 18-19).

Then the first half of the letter ends in praise. “Now to Him who is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine, according to His power that is at work within us, to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen” (verses 20-21).
passages.hearers:
Jews usually prayed standing. Kneeling showed special earnestness. Paul is on his knees, in chains, praying for people he may never see.

‘Every family derives its name’ is a play on words in Greek: Father is patēr, family is patria. Every family, in heaven and on earth, takes its name from the Father. Paul is saying that God is the source of all fatherhood, not a copy of human fathers. For readers whose fathers failed or hurt them, that matters. God is not like the worst father you have known. He is the Father every true fatherhood dimly reflects.

‘Rooted and grounded’ are pictures from gardening and building: a tree deep in the soil, a house on a firm foundation. Love is the soil and the foundation.

Notice the Trinity in the prayer: the Father hears, the Spirit strengthens, Christ dwells in the heart.

‘The length and width and height and depth’: Paul does not say of what at first. Readers have guessed the size of God's temple, or of his plan. Then he says it: the love of Christ. A love so large you can only know it by being filled with it.
passages.ot:
Solomon prayed on his knees at the temple's dedication, and asked, “will God indeed dwell upon the earth? Even heaven, the highest heaven, cannot contain You” (1 Kings 8:27). Paul prays that God will dwell by his Spirit in his people.

The psalms measure God's love by the heavens: “For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His loving devotion for those who fear Him” (Psalm 103:11). And no height or depth is beyond him: “If I ascend to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there” (Psalm 139:8).
passages.asks: Paul prays that his readers will know a love too large to know. Ask whether you believe Christ loves you, not in general, but you. If the word ‘father’ is hard for you, ask what it would mean that God is the Father from whom all true fatherhood comes. And try praying verses 16 to 19 for someone by name this week.
